name: Battery C, 62nd Coast Artillery (AA) / 62nd AAA Gun Bn
note: 1st Bn, 62nd CA (AA) became the 62nd AAA Gun Bn at Palermo; the battery's own reports switch name between Mar and Apr 1944.

name: Battery D, 106th AAA AW Bn (SP)
note: Kentucky National Guard (106th CA Bn (AA), Separate, until 1943). Attached to the 45th Infantry Division Aug 1944 - May 1945.

name: Medical Detachment, 67th Coast Artillery (AA) / 894th AAA AW Bn
note: The regiment's medical detachment: a regimental section with the Regimental HQ Battery and a section for each battalion, its men on special duty with the batteries. 2nd Bn, 67th CA (AA) became the 894th AAA AW Bn; the detachment reports as the 894th's by 19 Mar 1944. Its 1942-43 reports are book-type (roll 794, parts 2-3); March-April 1943 are missing.

name: Medical Detachment, 113th Infantry
note: New Jersey National Guard, inducted 16 Sep 1940 with the 44th Infantry Division. From December 1941 on coastal defense (the reports call the regiment RCT 113). The detachment's book-type reports (roll 1690, parts 2-3) give the station of its headquarters; it also had sections with the battalions, so a man's own post may differ.

name: Company G, 113th Infantry
note: 2nd Battalion, 113th Infantry: beach patrol on the Delaware coast (Bethany and Rehoboth Beaches) in 1943, then Port Republic, N.J., Fort Dix and Camp Pickett, Va. In April 1944 the company sent 16 of its NCOs and men as overseas replacements.

name: Company B, 313th Infantry (79th Infantry Division)
note: Its reports: Crown Hill Camp, Plymouth, 11-12 June 1944; aboard ship 13 June; Sébeville (inland from Utah Beach) 14 June; the drive on Cherbourg, which fell on 26 June; then south to the Ay river and the battle for La Haye-du-Puits in July. Stations give the nearest hamlet and a grid reference on the French Lambert Zone I grid, with a distance and bearing from the grid point.

name: HQ Battery, 128th AAA Gun Bn (Mbl)
note: A 90 mm gun battalion activated at Fort Bliss, Texas, on 20 May 1943. Third Army, as an army or corps battalion, from Normandy (late June 1944) to May 1945. Its headquarters ran the SCR-584 radar and the communications net. For 1945 the positions are the battalion's symbol on Third Army's antiaircraft situation maps.

name: 9th Armored Division
note: Activated 15 Jul 1942 at Fort Riley. The positions are the division's (or a combat command's), from its 1945 G.I. Stories booklet, Third Army's after action report and other division-level sources, and are drawn as assumed.
